title: Kafka Connect migration compatibility report, version 1
description: The report `conduit migrate kafka-connect` writes to report.json and returns as the `result` of its --json envelope (the envelope's `summary` is this document's `summary`). Contract: docs/design-documents/20261014-migrate-kafka-connect-mapping-and-harness.md, 'The compatibility report as a contract'. Hand-written, not reflected from Go types, so a struct change cannot silently change the contract. Adding a field, a code or an enum member is additive and keeps reportVersion 1; removing or renaming a field, or changing what status or blocking mean, bumps it. Consumers must ignore fields they do not know. The kc_migrate MCP tool returns this document as `result` and its generated files as a top-level `files` array beside it, never inside `result`.

generator.description: What produced the report: the Conduit version and every rule file used, with the upstream version it was written against.

summary.description: keys equals the number of entries, which equals the number of input key occurrences across all inputs (see entries for what an input key is); translated, approximated and unsupported partition keys; blocking counts blocking entries and blocking notes. The run is ok when blocking is 0.

connectors.description: One element per connector, in input order, and one per worker file (role worker).

acceptedGaps.description: Blocking entries and notes that --accept-gaps let through. Empty without that flag.

code.description: A stable error or finding code in domain.reason form, for example kc.key_unsupported.

origin.description: Where a key is in the input: line and column (1-based) for properties, a JSON pointer for JSON. file is relative to the common parent of all inputs, with forward slashes; <stdin> for standard input. Never carries a value.

pipeline.description: Generated pipeline file, relative to the output directory. Absent when none is written.

certification.description: Certification tier per emitted plugin, read from the registry index at run time.

entries.description: One per input key occurrence, in origin order. An input key is a connector config key: a .properties key, a member of config in the REST form, a member of a bare config map, or a member of info.config in a REST export. The wrapper members (the REST form's top-level name, type, tasks and initial_state; an export's map key, info.name, info.type, info.tasks and status) are not config keys and have no entry; they set connectors[].name and the pipeline status. The earlier of two duplicate keys has code kc.key_duplicate.

notes.description: Differences with no input key (absent-key defaults, output shape, delivery semantics, required settings, and kc.converter_unknown when neither the connector nor the worker file sets key.converter or value.converter, blocking, one note per missing converter). Not part of the completeness multiset.

transforms.description: Index of the SMT chain. Each SMT sub-key also has its own entry.

resume.description: How the pipeline starts relative to the original connector's position (Debezium Postgres offset import, docs/design-documents/20261012-migrate-debezium-postgres-offset-import.md).

outputCompat.description: Debezium-compatible output mode, when the pipeline uses it (docs/design-documents/20261012-debezium-compatible-output.md).

differences.description: Ids of the intentional differences that apply to this config.

configPath.description: JSON pointer into the generated pipeline file.

env.description: Environment variable a secret was replaced with.

rule.description: The rule that emitted the note.
